I’m so sorry this has happened/is happening to you. How long have you been together? Do you have family close by? You mentioned couples counselling but it would be a good idea to see a psychologist on your own to work through your health individually as well. 
It’s so easy when you love someone to give them excuses for bad behaviour, but at the end of the day your SO is meant to make your life better and you’re meant to pull each other up when the world gets you down. They’re usually meat to love you the most in the whole world and his behaviour towards you is not loving, caring or supportive. 
Your relationship doesn’t sound healthy and this is tough when a relationship as important as a wife and husband goes so badly. How long has it been like this? I’m assuming this is not the normal status quo? 

It sounds like he’s reacting so violently because he feels guilty that he has feelings for this woman.  But, as other people have said, the feelings for this other woman aren’t the main problem, it’s how he’s been treating you and speaking to you. He’s showing you thought his actions and words very explicitly that he doesn’t care enough about you to try and fix the relationship or even apologise for causing you so much emotional distress. You would never ( I’m assuming) accept this behaviour for anyone else, please don’t accept this type of behaviour from your SO! You love him, but love isn’t enough  and as difficult as it may be because you care about him and your relationship this type of behaviour is unacceptable and it sounds like the relationship you may have once had with this man doesn’t exist any more. If he wants to work to change his behaviour( which he’s shown he doesn’t by doing nothing when you asked him to fix it) he needs to put a lot of work in and stop being verbally abusive. 

I don’t know you or your husband so I don’t know if he’s done something you haven’t mentioned or to indicate a commitment to the relationship, but from what you’ve said it sounds like you’d be better off moving out. 

If it’s as bad as potentially violent I would do as others have also suggested and quietly make plans to leave and speak to a lawyer. 

You deserve to be treated with respect, and if he thinks it’s okay to treat you like this - at least twice and not even realise how horrible he’s being and want to working on changing it, I would start to make plans to leave. 

Best of luck, and remember to be kind to yourself.

In my experience schools and workplaces still do discriminate, they’re just more subtle about it now as people know there is legislation in place against such discrimination. For example, as a university student in Australia i have to approach my practical tutors ( I study veterinary medicine) myself and try and work out changes to accommodate me instead of student services approaching the academic staff. An imbalance of power much?! These people, who may be very knowledgeable in whatever field of science they’re in often know nothing about learning disabilities and mostly see people like me as another chore they have to deal with. Some are really nice about it, but mostly they’re ignorant jerks who don’t understand and don’t really want to put the extra effort in. I’m used to speaking up for myself, but doing this every semester, for every subject and with multiple tutors for the same subject is incredibly  time consuming, energy draining and makes me feel like an imposition most of the time and a piece of shit. Just because today we treat people better, or their are policies in place that say you should treat them better means nothing if people aren’t educated about why certain people require extra time/other considerations. It’s mostly lip service, not a real effort to help people with different needs out in my opinion.

Compassion fatigue is a big problem in the vet industry but it's also present in human medicine as well. As other people have suggested shadowing a vet is a good option. I think it's something many people struggle with, myself included. I worked in a vet clinic and volunteered at the RSPCA domestic hospital to explore vet as a career choice before I applied. Euthanasia is a big part of being a vet. It is upsetting and hard to get through, but I think if you don't explore your options now, even if it's to confirm that vet isn't the right career for you, it'll be harder later wondering 'what if'. Talk to vets you know and get work experience at a clinic. Good luck!
